not_tested.reason: input cannot establish focus order and visibility

summary.perceived_purpose: Sign-up screen for a personal budgeting app with a plan choice.
summary.first_impression: Clean and friendly, but the three plan cards read as decoration rather than a choice.
summary.headline: Clear purpose; plan selection is easy to miss and price text is hard to read.

findings.title: Suspected insufficient text contrast on plan price labels
findings.observed: Grey price text on a white card samples at about 2.9:1 in the screenshot.
findings.expected: At least 4.5:1 for body-size text, or 3:1 if the text qualifies as large.
findings.impact: Users with low vision or in bright light may not read the price before committing; the plan choice step is degraded. Priority P0 because the fix is a one-line color token change on the primary flow.

evidence.note: Sampled from screenshot pixels; rendered font size unknown

findings.recommendation: Use a darker color token for price text; keep the light tint for secondary labels only.
findings.code_guidance: Raise the price label color token until it meets 4.5:1 against the card background; verify at the rendered size.

steps: Measure the contrast of the price labels at rendered size using computed colors.
retest.expected_result: Ratio at least 4.5:1, or at least 3:1 with the text qualifying as large.

findings.limitations: Ratio estimated from screenshot pixels; rendered font size unknown, so the large-text exception could not be evaluated; the check is reported as PARTIAL.

findings.title: Primary action competes with the plan cards for attention
findings.location: scr_1 (uploaded screenshot), hero and plan cards
findings.observed: The 'Get started' button and three equally saturated plan cards carry similar visual weight; the eye path lands on the cards first.
findings.expected: One dominant primary action, with the plan choice clearly subordinate or clearly presented as a required step.
findings.impact: First-time users hesitate between the cards and the button; the sign-up task starts slower and may begin with a wrong tap.

evidence.note: Salience estimate over the captured viewport

findings.recommendation: Lower the plan cards' saturation and add the caption 'Choose a plan', or move plan selection to the step after 'Get started'.

steps: Re-run the first_impression and primary_action tests with the same presets on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: Simulated personas name 'Get started' as the first element they notice and would tap.

findings.limitations: Salience inferred from a static screenshot; motion, hover states, and scroll position are unknown.

findings.title: Simulated personas did not recognize the plan selector as a choice
findings.observed: 2 of 3 simulated personas described the plan cards as informational and expected 'Get started' to proceed without a plan choice.
findings.expected: Personas identify the plan cards as a required choice before continuing.
findings.impact: Users may proceed without choosing a plan and be surprised by a default selection.

persona_signals.observation: The plan cards look like feature highlights.
Unsure whether tapping a card does anything.

findings.recommendation: Make the plan cards read as a selectable group: a visible selected state, single-choice semantics, and a caption such as 'Choose a plan'.

steps: Re-run the primary_action and comprehension tests with the same three presets on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: At least 2 of 3 simulated personas identify the plan cards as a choice.

findings.limitations: Simulated persona behavior from a static screenshot; not human participant research.

findings.title: Terms text under the button is unlikely to be read
findings.location: scr_1 (uploaded screenshot), below the primary button
findings.observed: A two-line legal notice in small light text sits directly under 'Get started'.
findings.expected: Legal consequences of the primary action are visible before the action, or the notice is short and legible.
findings.impact: Users may accept terms without noticing; low user impact, some trust and compliance risk.
findings.recommendation: Shorten the notice to one line at body size and link to the full terms.

steps: Check the notice text size and position on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: Notice is one line at body text size, above or beside the button.

findings.limitations: Text size estimated from a static screenshot; rendered size unknown.
